chapters.title: The One Thing
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 1 introduces the governing idea through the City Slickers frame, overextension, uneven focus, and the claim that the most important task makes other work easier or unnecessary.
chapters.coreMove: Name the single concern or task that carries the most leverage before spending energy anywhere else.
chapters.commonMisread: Telling the reader to choose one favorite task and ignore the rest.

chapters.title: The Domino Effect
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 2 adds sequence to leverage: large outcomes grow through cumulative domino actions where one right move creates conditions for the next.
chapters.coreMove: Find the first small action whose completion knocks the next necessary action into reach.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating success as a single heroic leap or a generic list of baby steps.

chapters.title: Success Leaves Clues
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 3 says successful outcomes leave studyable patterns, while warning against copying every surface detail or treating success as magic.
chapters.coreMove: Study a strong outcome for transferable patterns while refusing to copy its surface costume.
chapters.commonMisread: Imitating successful people detail for detail or turning winners into proof of certainty.

chapters.title: Everything Matters Equally
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 1 begins by dismantling the lie that everything matters equally and pushes the reader from task democracy toward sharper ranking.
chapters.coreMove: Break task democracy by ranking work according to leverage, not neatness, urgency, or volume.
chapters.commonMisread: Repeating the 80/20 idea as a slogan without forcing a hard ranking.

chapters.title: Multitasking
chapters.sourcePressure: This lie chapter rejects multitasking as false productivity, focusing on divided attention, switching, error risk, and the prestige of appearing busy on several fronts.
chapters.coreMove: Stop treating attention switching as extra capacity and return to one consequential task at a time.
chapters.commonMisread: Saying phones are distracting or that people should generally focus more.

chapters.title: A Disciplined Life
chapters.sourcePressure: This lie chapter rejects the fantasy of a universally disciplined life and points toward selective consistency around the one behavior that matters most.
chapters.coreMove: Trade the fantasy of total self-control for one narrow discipline repeated until it becomes dependable.
chapters.commonMisread: Preaching stricter character, universal toughness, or a perfect lifestyle.

chapters.title: Willpower Is Always on Will-Call
chapters.sourcePressure: This lie chapter rejects the idea that willpower is always available and teaches the reader to place high-value work where energy and freshness are strongest.
chapters.coreMove: Schedule the most important work for the part of the day when restraint and freshness are actually available.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating willpower as a personality trait or making claims about biology the source does not support.

chapters.title: A Balanced Life
chapters.sourcePressure: This lie chapter rejects static balance and teaches purposeful, temporary imbalance when one responsibility or season requires extra force.
chapters.coreMove: Accept deliberate imbalance for a season while naming what must be protected and repaired afterward.
chapters.commonMisread: Making a generic work-life balance speech or excusing permanent neglect.

chapters.title: Big Is Bad
chapters.sourcePressure: This lie chapter challenges suspicion toward large aims while keeping scale tied to legitimacy rather than fantasy or dream-big rhetoric.
chapters.coreMove: Question the reflex that shrinks goals for comfort, then test whether a larger aim is legitimate and actionable.
chapters.commonMisread: Pumping the reader up to dream big without standards or limits.

chapters.title: The Focusing Question
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 2 introduces the Focusing Question as the operational tool for leverage: narrow toward the next consequential move without pretending certainty is guaranteed.
chapters.coreMove: Use one leverage question to narrow from many possible moves to the next move that changes the rest.
chapters.commonMisread: Quoting a slogan and treating it as a magic answer generator.

chapters.title: The Success Habit
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 2 turns the Focusing Question into a repeated success habit, centered on asking for leverage often enough that it changes decisions.
chapters.coreMove: Make leverage-seeking a repeated habit so decisions keep narrowing before busyness takes over.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating habit as routine for its own sake or repeating generic habit advice.

chapters.title: The Path to Great Answers
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 2 shifts from asking the question to finding stronger answers through serious search, while avoiding perfectionist delay.
chapters.coreMove: Push past the first adequate answer by searching seriously for the answer that changes the standard.
chapters.commonMisread: Confusing great answers with endless research or perfectionist delay.

chapters.title: Live With Purpose
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 3 connects focus to purpose as the larger direction that gives the one thing meaning, without letting purpose stay vague.
chapters.coreMove: Turn focus toward a larger direction clear enough to judge what deserves your one thing.
chapters.commonMisread: Letting purpose become inspirational fog or a substitute for hard priority choices.

chapters.title: Live By Priority
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 3 turns purpose into priority, the ordered first claim that prevents many worthy items from remaining equally active.
chapters.coreMove: Translate purpose into one ordered first claim that tells every other worthy claim to wait.
chapters.commonMisread: Sorting a to-do list while keeping many priorities equally alive.

chapters.title: Live for Productivity
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 3 turns priority into productivity, defined as concentrated execution of the chosen first claim rather than busyness or output theater.
chapters.coreMove: Carry the chosen priority into protected execution where visible output follows from focused action.
chapters.commonMisread: Equating productivity with busyness, speed, or a larger count of completed tasks.

chapters.title: The Three Commitments
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 3 frames the three commitments as protections for sustained focus over time, not blind stubbornness or intensity theater.
chapters.coreMove: Protect the chosen path with commitments that keep learning, ownership, and accountability attached to focused work.
chapters.commonMisread: Confusing commitment with stubborn intensity or inventing unsupported rigid rules.

chapters.title: The Four Thieves
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 3 identifies recurring thieves that remove time, structure, or attention from the chosen path and asks for practical defenses instead of paranoia.
chapters.coreMove: Identify the recurring threats that steal protected focus and build defenses before they enter the room.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning obstacles into vague anxiety, blame, or a made-up canonical list.

chapters.title: The Journey
chapters.sourcePressure: Part 3 closes by treating one-thing discipline as an ongoing journey and lived practice, not a neat finish line or vague uplift.
chapters.coreMove: Treat the one-thing discipline as a continuing path of repeated choices rather than a finished achievement.
chapters.commonMisread: Ending with vague inspiration, a tidy recap, or a brand-new framework.
